newsitem.title: FRANCE: RALLYING-PANIZZI OPENS UP EARLY LEAD IN TOUR OF CORSICA.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-PANIZZI OPENS UP EARLY LEAD IN TOUR OF CORSICA.

text.p: Frenchman Gilles Panizzi, driving a Peugeot 306, upstaged the favourites to take an early lead in the Tour of Corsica rally on Monday.
Panizzi, who came a surprise third in last month's Catalunya rally, was six seconds ahead of compatriot Francois Delecour, also in a two-wheel drive Peugeot, after the first two timed stages.
Briton Colin McRae clocked the fastest time in his Subaru Impreza in the first stretch over 25.5 kms from Verghia to Pietra Rossa, in the mountains south of Ajaccio.
But Panizzi and Delecour, who lost one second and six seconds respectively in that section, took charge in the next, over 22.6 kms from Filitosa to Bicchisiano.
French champion Panizzi was fastest with Delecour one second slower while McRae could manage only the seventh fastest time, losing 14 seconds on Panizzi.
McRae, the 1995 world champion, was third overall 13 seconds behind the leader.

World champion Tommi Makinen of Finland, who won the last two rallies in Portugal and Spain in his Mitsubishi Lancer, was a modest sixth, 17 seconds behind Panizzi, with four timed stages remaining in the first day of the three-day event.
